simple.meaning: פַּס (paç) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a long and sleeved tunic (perhaps simply a wide one; from the original sense of the root, i.e. of many breadths).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 37:3. The surrounding context includes family, family line, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פַּס (H6446) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a long and sleeved tunic (perhaps simply a wide one; from the original sense of the root, i.e. of many breadths)
definitions.full: H6446. pas [ מַּס ] noun [masculine] flat of hand or foot (palm, sole); — only מַּסִּים כְּתֹנֶת tunic reaching to palms and soles (see ׳כ ) Gen 37:3 , 23 , 32 ; 2Sam 13:18-19 , (compare Dr). פסס (√of following; see Biblical Hebrew I. פסס , [ מַּס ]).
definitions.rootNote: from 6461 ; properly, the palm (of the hand) or sole (of the foot) (compare 6447 ); by implication (plural)

occurrences.englishText: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.
When Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of many colors that was on him;
They took the tunic of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, “We have found this. Examine it, now, and see if it is your son’s tunic or not.”
She had a garment of various colors on her; for the king’s daughters who were virgins dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and went her way, crying aloud as she went.
